Why aren't knee and elbow pads built into military trousers and blouses?

They were when I was in the army. You had velcro pouches at the elbows and knees that you could insert knee and elbow pads into them. This was around 2004 so maybe they took that functionality out of the ACUs (or whatever they are using now) but it did at one point exist.

Problem was that they sucked and mostly we just didn't wear them. I would prefer to drop to a knee without a knee pad than to have a thin knee pad that I had to put up with all patrol. Elbow pads are about useless unless you are going to be on your elbows for awhile which is not that common a phenomenon for your average soldier.

They need to fit tighter than clothing usually does, and ill fitting protective pads would actually increase the injury risk. It also saves money because pads and clothing are easier to handle and maintain on their own. Never mind that not everybody needs protective pads all the time.

They would have to have a lot more sizes of uniforms based on arm and leg length to have the pads cover the appropriate areas on people who are either taller or shorter than average. It is a lot easier and cheaper to just have a few sizes of uniforms, and then just have a few sizes of pads that go over the uniform. Plus if the pads are built in, when the uniform or the pads wear out, you have to replace both.
